summary_rationale: Astra Microwave possesses genuine, hard-to-replicate RF/microwave qualification moats (30 MHz–40 GHz, in-house 17m NFTR and NABL EMI/EMC chambers, ISRO space-grade certification, and the 50:50 Astra Rafael Comsys JV, which accelerated to ₹334 Cr H1 FY27 revenue and ₹913 Cr backlog) that have propelled consolidated backlog to ₹4,708 Cr in Q2 FY27 (99.2% domestic defence in standalone) and expanded OPM from 12% in FY22 to 29% in FY26 (33% in Q2 FY27) with ROCE at 20.3%, alongside Oct 29, 2026 BSE/NSE clearance for the 1:1 Astra Space Technologies demerger. However, the business remains structurally cyclical, customer-concentrated (~47% of standalone backlog in one ₹1,844 Cr ex-GST HAL Uttam AESA radar contract; >50% of FY26 sales from DRDO and BEL/DPSUs; 11.9% exports largely deemed exports to ARC), and working-capital intensive: it carries a 537-day cash conversion cycle (216 debtor days, 394 inventory days), generated -₹46 Cr cumulative 12-year Free Cash Flow across FY15–FY26, swung back to -₹147.85 Cr operating cash flow in H1 FY27 (lifting debt to ₹487 Cr), carries ~₹196 Cr in FY26 year-end receivables from ARC plus ₹80 Cr in JV guarantees (with ECL on receivables flagged as a Key Audit Matter), relies on ₹130.50 Cr in pending June 2025 warrant conversion proceeds due December 29, 2026, and operates with a low 6.54% promoter stake alongside a 0.41% Q2 FY27 stake trim by Whole-Time Director Atim Kabra.
